steps.title: High acidity
steps.body: Furmint gives whites with very high acidity and flavours of lemon, green apple, quince, pear, smoke and a mineral, flinty edge. With age or botrytis, honey, apricot and marmalade appear. Body ranges from medium to full; alcohol can be high in dry styles.

steps.title: Origins and noble rot
steps.body: Furmint is Hungary's signature grape, probably native to the Tokaj region; it's also grown in Slovenia as Šipon. It ripens late, which keeps acidity high. Its thin skins become thinner as it ripens, making it highly susceptible to noble rot, Botrytis cinerea. That's why it's the main grape of Tokaji Aszú.

steps.prompt: Why is Furmint so suited to noble rot?
options: Its skins thin as it ripens

steps.title: Spotting it
steps.body: Dry Furmint is pale lemon, with citrus, quince and smoky, flinty notes, high acidity and a firm, mineral palate. Sweet Tokaji is gold to amber, with apricot, marmalade and honey, balanced by vivid acidity. That acidity is the common thread.

steps.explanation: Not true. Its very high acidity is its signature.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Furmint has very high acidity, with quince and smoke
It's native to Tokaj and susceptible to noble rot
Its acidity links dry and sweet styles
